PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-10-12
19M, general wellness examination.

S:
Patient presents for a wellness visit as he transitions to adult care. He reports feeling generally well with good energy, playing recreational soccer twice a week. Denies chest pain. Diet includes frequent sugary drinks and energy drinks, which was discussed. He is a college student working part time at a cafe. Mother with breast cancer. Appetite is good and sleep is about 7 hours most nights. Lives with roommates. Never smoker, occasional alcohol.

O:
BP 118/72, HR 66, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 168 lb, BMI 24.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
Neck: no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Extremities: no edema, pulses intact.
Labs (prior week): Hgb 12.7 g/dL, A1c 5.9%, fasting glucose 100 mg/dL, basic metabolic panel normal.

A/P:
1. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary and energy drinks and continuing regular soccer and walking. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
2. Anemia, stable on recheck. Continue oral iron daily with vitamin C. Repeat CBC in 3 months.
3. Family history: reviewed relevant family history with patient and discussed reassurance and routine follow-up.
4. Health maintenance: immunizations reviewed and updated as needed. Counseled on alcohol moderation, consistent sleep, and hydration, especially around sports and study schedules. Encouraged continued physical activity and balanced meals.
5. Lifestyle: discussed limiting caffeine from energy drinks and planning regular meals during busy study periods.

Return in 6 months to review labs, sooner as needed.
